data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Separation is necessary because a single engine's 'verification' is actually a 'consistency check' of its own internal probability distribution, which is fundamentally incapable of discovering 'unknown unknowns' present in its own training priors.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The model is capable of 'self-correction' through symbolic execution (code) that bypasses probabilistic priors.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The training data is so exhaustive that the 'blind spots' are negligible for the problem domain.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A single model's authoring and checking phases are both sampled from the same conditional probability distribution P(Output | Prompt). Even with different prompts, the underlying priors (the 'blind spots') are identical. Independent verification requires a second distribution Q(Output | Prompt) with different training data, ensuring that the intersection of their error sets is minimized. Evidence of restatement is a 'Zero-Correction Convergence' where the checker finds no errors in a claim that is later proven false by an external engine.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
